description: Interior of Japan's House of Representatives chamber in the National Diet Building, Tokyo: long rows of wooden desks with microphones facing a central rostrum and presiding officer's chair, ornate wood panelling, wide-angle photograph.
Chamber of Japan's House of Councillors: semicircular tiers of green seats around a central podium, wood-panelled walls, formal parliamentary photograph.
The Kantei in Tokyo, official residence of the Prime Minister of Japan: modern five-storey glass and stone building with a gently curved Japanese-style roof, photographed from the front garden.
Tokyo Imperial Palace: white Edo-period style keep and stone walls beyond the Nijubashi double-arched bridge over a moat, pine trees, clear day.
The State Duma building in Moscow: grand early-20th-century classical facade with columns on Okhotny Ryad street, daytime photograph.
The Federation Council building on Bolshaya Dmitrovka Street, Moscow: pale neoclassical facade with a portico, Russian flag above the entrance.
The Moscow Kremlin: red walls and towers, the Senate Palace dome flying the Russian presidential standard, seen from across Red Square at golden hour.
Political map of Germany divided into its sixteen federal states (Länder), each state in a different colour and labelled with its name, on a clean white background.
The Luxembourg Palace in Paris: elegant 17th-century palace facade with a central dome, formal gardens and fountain in the foreground.
A leather-bound volume of the French Constitution of 1958 with gold lettering and a blue-white-red ribbon marker, resting on a wooden desk.
The Élysée Palace in Paris: neoclassical facade viewed from the gravel courtyard, French and European flags, Republican Guards.
The Hôtel Matignon in Paris: refined 18th-century hôtel particulier with pale stone facade, slate roof and manicured garden.
The Supreme Court of Canada building in Ottawa: granite art-deco and château-style building with steep green copper roofs, statues in front.

An outdoor state ceremony on Parliament Hill, Ottawa in April 1982: Queen Elizabeth II seated at a table signing a large constitutional document, Canadian officials standing behind, Peace Tower in the background.
The Supreme Court of India building in New Delhi: long curved Indo-British facade with a central dome, red sandstone and cream plaster, lawns in front.
Courtroom No. 1 of the Supreme Court of India: dark wood-panelled chamber, a high elevated bench for the judges, rows of lawyers' desks, solemn atmosphere.
A long queue of Indian voters of all ages outside a polling station on election day, holding voter ID cards, one voter proudly showing an indelible-ink-marked finger.
The Marriner S. Eccles Building in Washington, D.C.: monumental limestone headquarters of the Federal Reserve with tall windows and an eagle sculpture above the entrance.
The Bank of England on Threadneedle Street, London: imposing neoclassical facade with Corinthian columns and the statue of the Duke of Wellington nearby.
British money: gold-and-silver one-pound coins and colourful polymer Bank of England notes (£5, £10, £20) fanned out on a dark surface, top-down photograph.
